clue.text: Copper's arresting deed, beginning to search plant

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the copper symbol holds the deed inside it

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a deed is an act

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A policeman detains a man for some deed before starting a search of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the element whose symbol is Cu; 'arresting' puts ACT inside CU, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny desert succulent, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Article absorbing female drained of colour

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the article holds the female inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece soaks up a woman until she has lost her colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face gone grey and pale, as with fear or illness.

clue.text: To protect oneself, acquire insurance

definitions.meaning: to shelter from danger, as under fire
to obtain cover, the insurer's word for a policy's protection

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to shelter from danger and to buy an insurance policy's cover.

clue.text: Southern Greek character cross about knight and mythical monster

indicators.note: about means around, so the Greek letter and the cross go round the knight

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
X is the shape of a cross
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A Greek from the south crosses a knight over some legendary beast.
explanation.walkthrough: PHI and X together go 'about' N, giving PHINX after S.
explanation.definitionFit: The sphinx of legend is a winged creature with a lion's body and a human head.

clue.text: Run through train

definitions.meaning: to go over something in practice before doing it
to drill or practise ahead of a performance

explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance, which is both running through it and training for it.

clue.text: Two calls ensued about a second game

indicators.note: about means around, so the two calls surround the letter a

parts.note: a ring is a telephone call, and two of them give two copies
the second of the two calls, another ring
ensued means followed, or arose

explanation.surface: Two phone calls came in around a second, in some sort of game.
explanation.walkthrough: The two RINGs go 'about' A, giving RINGARING, then AROSE and S follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's ring game played with a nursery rhyme, ending with everyone falling down.

clue.text: Weed round front of semi with instrument, gardening aid

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the weeding word goes about the next letter

parts.note: to hoe is to weed the soil with a hoe

indicators.note: front of says take only the first letter of semi

parts.note: a pipe is a simple wind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone weeds around a semi-detached house while playing music, using a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts S, the front of 'semi', inside HOE. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flexible tube used to water plants is an everyday garden tool.

clue.text: Member's brought in beer, more than enough

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the member goes into the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has had beer brought in, more than he needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, with enough and to spare.

clue.text: Parted sides to reveal damaged hair

parts.note: parted means split apart
the ends of something are its sides or extremities

explanation.surface: Hair parted at the sides shows how damaged it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair whose tips have frayed into two strands is hair with damage.

clue.text: Greet 28 shipworkers

parts.note: the answer to 28 across is a tremor, which is a shake
hands are sailors working aboard a ship

explanation.surface: A clue cross-referring to another, about greeting a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The '28' means take the answer to 28 across, TREMOR, and use a synonym of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and pumping someone's palm is a common way of greeting them.

clue.text: Whitish heraldic stripe

definitions.meaning: in heraldry, a vertical band down the centre of a shield

explanation.definitionFit: The word means light in colour and also names a vertical band in coats of arms.

clue.text: Snake in Canada coiled round leg

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go about the leg
coiled means twisted around, so the letters of the country are rearranged

parts.note: the on side, or leg side, in cricket is ON

explanation.surface: A snake in Canada wraps itself round someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coiled' shuffles the country to ANACDA, and 'round' wraps that about the leg. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constrictor, a kind of snake.

clue.text: Italian river engulfing remainder at once

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the river holds the remainder

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: An Italian river swallows up what is left in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a magician's word for immediately, as in hey presto.

clue.text: Some jet-ski everywhere in this place in eastern Europe

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Jet-skis are everywhere in some city in eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in this', but a city name cannot stand for 'in this place'; 'in this' is a link and the definition is 'place in eastern Europe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now usually Kyiv, is the capital of Ukraine, a city in eastern Europe.

clue.text: Unscripted, I am sharp for all to see

parts.note: I'm is the shortened form of I am
sharp means prompt, on time, as in six o'clock sharp
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be quick-witted and visible to everyone, speaking off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, without preparation.

clue.text: Cheeky rascal, pupil throwing stone

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: throwing means casting off, so the stone is removed

parts.note: a student is a pupil
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A naughty child is a cheeky pupil who throws stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' takes ST off STUDENT, leaving UDENT. ST is a stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent means rudely disrespectful, much the same as cheeky.

clue.text: First to discreetly mention removing cap to show respect

indicators.note: first to says take only the opening letter of the next word
the cap is the top, so the opening letter is taken off

parts.note: a reference is a mention

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly tips their cap as a mark of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing cap' drops the opening letter of the mention, leaving EFERENCE; 'cap' is the top letter, not headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is polite submission to another, a show of regard.

clue.text: Twelve, perhaps, not very bright climbing thing abroad

indicators.note: climbing means going up, so in a down clue the word reads backwards

parts.note: dim means not very bright, of light or of wits

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted thing climbs abroad, perhaps at twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns DIM into MID, and 'abroad' rearranges THING as NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is one example of the hour named; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Fair game at home? Good

parts.note: a game is a sport
in means at home

explanation.surface: Is a game played at home a fair one? Good.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting gesture is a fair and generous one, as from a good loser.

clue.text: Eat nothing when wrapped in paper

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so the word for when goes inside the paper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Eat nothing when it comes wrapped in newspaper, like fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food for a time.

clue.text: Mimic arrives on board vessel

indicators.note: on board means inside a vessel, so the arrival goes inside the pot

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: A mimic arrives aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words without understanding, mimicking them.

clue.text: Bird out, flying about, with tail of green

indicators.note: flying means moving freely about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for circa, about

indicators.note: tail of says take only the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A bird is out, flying about with a green tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' shuffles out to TOU; 'about' is not a container signal here but circa, the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird with a huge, brightly coloured bill.

clue.text: Pulled up chasing evasive rodent

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the reversed piece comes after

parts.note: coy means evasive, reluctant to commit

indicators.note: pulled means drawn back, so in a down clue the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up while chasing an elusive rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled' reads the word up backwards, giving PU; 'chasing' puts it after the evasive word.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Adore car prepared for rally

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loves a car made ready for a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the seven letters of ADORE and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a motor race held over public roads.

clue.text: Search round for small band

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Searching around for a little band of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small jazz or dance band.

clue.text: Nimble agent crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the agent spans the river

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A nimble secret agent crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means active and lively, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Beginning to grasp one branch of physics, and the science of food

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: astronomy is a physical science, the study of the stars

explanation.surface: Beginning to grasp physics, then the science of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the art and study of good eating.

clue.text: Distinguished American statesman of old

parts.note: august means distinguished, dignified

explanation.surface: A distinguished American statesman from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, a ruler of the ancient world.

clue.text: In centre, moral majority could make one quake

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A moral majority at the centre could shake things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is found across the end of centre and the start of moral.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking, especially of the earth.
